sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your Twenties, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨二十岁时经历的一些重大人生变化和过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你在世界的哪个角落。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要继续剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: If nothing else, our 20s are this kind of beautiful time of transformation and reinvention.
sentences.zh: 如果说二十岁有什么意义，那就是它是一个充满蜕变和重塑的美好时期。

sentences.en: That is a universal truth, a universal statement for me that each of us, no matter what we're going through, what we're struggling with, what we do or don't achieve,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一个普遍真理，一个普遍的陈述，即我们每个人，无论正在经历什么，在为什么而挣扎，无论取得了什么成就或未取得什么成就，

sentences.en: we will have to rediscover time and time again who we are.
sentences.zh: 我们都必须一次又一次地重新发现自己是谁。

sentences.en: And we also have to rediscover how far off that is from who we want to be probably hundreds of times during this period of emerging adulthood.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个成年初期，我们可能还要数百次地重新发现自己与理想中的自我之间有多大的差距。

sentences.en: We spend so much of childhood and also our teenage years being the person that others want us to be or rebelling against this version entirely
sentences.zh: 我们花费了童年和青少年时期的大部分时间去成为别人希望我们成为的人，或者完全反抗这种版本，

sentences.en: to carve out what we think is our own space.
sentences.zh: 以开辟出我们认为属于自己的空间。

sentences.en: And I think our 20s is when we start to find balance and we really get the chance to do that all over again and independently.
sentences.zh: 我认为二十岁是我们开始寻找平衡的时候，我们真的有机会独立地重新做这一切。

sentences.en: And we approach, you know, self-discovery with a new maturity and a new sense of truth.
sentences.zh: 我们以一种新的成熟度和新的真实感来对待自我发现。

sentences.en: Things about us become a lot more clear.
sentences.zh: 关于我们的事情变得清晰多了。

sentences.en: And what we're likely to experience is a bit of a metamorphosis and a shedding of the old into the new.
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会经历某种蜕变，从旧我向新我蜕变。

sentences.en: This is definitely a rite of passage and sometimes it's deeply uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一种成长仪式，有时会让人感到非常不舒服。

sentences.en: But when you get to the point of not really enjoying your life, not liking who you are, not knowing what you stand for, what your dreams are, who you even want to be,
sentences.zh: 但当你到了那种不再真正享受生活、不喜欢自己、不知道自己坚持什么、梦想是什么、甚至不知道自己想成为什么样的人的时候，

sentences.en: you are really, I think, called to a place of reinvention.
sentences.zh: 我认为你真的被召唤到一个需要重塑自我的境地。

sentences.en: And that is what I want to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我今天想谈的话题。

sentences.en: How can we reinvent and rediscover ourselves in our 20s when things start to feel stagnant or off or we start to feel a sense of disconnection
sentences.zh: 当事情开始感到停滞或不对劲，或者我们开始感到一种脱节感时，我们如何在二十岁时重塑和重新发现自己，

sentences.en: between who we are right now and who we really want to be?
sentences.zh: 即现在的我们与我们真正想成为的人之间的脱节？

sentences.en: How do we kind of shake things up?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何打破现状？

sentences.en: How do we find our path?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何找到自己的道路？

sentences.en: How do we have that refresh where we fall back in love with our lives through our old actions?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何通过旧有的行动重新爱上我们的生活，实现那种焕然一新？

sentences.en: Well, we are going to talk through five tips that you can work through either step by step or you can kind of choose one or the other for reinvention during this decade.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们将讨论五个技巧，你可以一步步实践，或者选择其中一个来在这个十年里实现重塑。

sentences.en: This includes some methods for visualizing your next chapter and how to use psychology to really motivate yourself to get there,
sentences.zh: 这包括一些构想你下一个篇章的方法，以及如何利用心理学真正激励自己去实现目标，

sentences.en: how to use psychology to motivate a sense of confidence.
sentences.zh: 如何利用心理学来激发自信心。

sentences.en: Also, how we can use that discomfort, use the boredom, the isolation, the stagnation, the uncertainty in our favor rather than fighting against it.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们如何利用这种不适感，利用无聊、孤立、停滞、不确定性来为我们所用，而不是与之对抗。

sentences.en: How can we actually take all of those things that are making us crave reinvention
sentences.zh: 我们如何真正利用所有那些让我们渴望重塑的事物，

sentences.en: and help us get there rather than kind of, I don't know, burden us?
sentences.zh: 来帮助我们实现目标，而不是让它们成为我们的负担？

sentences.en: We are also going to discuss the power of risk and this construct called the timeline for change and how to shift from very anxious what-if thinking
sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论风险的力量，以及这个被称为“改变时间表”的结构，以及如何从焦虑的“万一”思维，

sentences.en: to a what-else-or-so-what mentality, which is honestly one of my favorite ways to think about this.
sentences.zh: 转变为“还有什么”或“那又怎样”的心态，老实说，这是我最喜欢的思考方式之一。

sentences.en: One of my favorite ideas in this space is that switch, that mental and cognitive switch from seeing things in a disaster scenario lens or from a disaster scenario lens
sentences.zh: 在这个领域，我最喜欢的想法之一就是那种转变，那种从灾难性视角看待事物的心理和认知转换，

sentences.en: to an abundant lens, from an abundant position of excess and authenticity and growth.
sentences.zh: 转变为一种丰盛的视角，从一种充盈、真实和成长的丰盛立场出发。

sentences.en: I've got to say this is one of my favorite episodes that I've done as of recent because it just combines all my favorite nuggets of advice and theories into one package
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这是我最近做过的最喜欢的节目之一，因为它把我所有最喜欢的建议和理论精华结合在了一个包里，

sentences.en: and truly it really represents so much of my philosophy towards this period in our lives.
sentences.zh: 它确实代表了我对我们人生这一阶段的很大一部分哲学。

sentences.en: You know, our 20s are for exploration.
sentences.zh: 你知道，二十岁是用来探索的。

sentences.en: They are for reinvention,
sentences.zh: 它是用来重塑的，

sentences.en: rebuilding, transformation more so than any other time.
sentences.zh: 重建、转型，比任何其他时期都更重要。

sentences.en: So I really want us to be able to unlock that for ourselves even if it's through small steps, even if it's not as drastic as you're picturing.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的希望我们能为自己解锁这一点，即使是通过小步骤，即使它不像你想象的那么剧烈。

sentences.en: Also, I guess whenever I get the opportunity to talk about risk and our approach to uncertainty, that is like a favorite topic of mine because it's something that I deeply,
sentences.zh: 另外，我想每当我有机会谈论风险和我们对待不确定性的态度时，那都是我最喜欢的话题之一，因为我深深地认为，

sentences.en: deeply think is important that we stop seeing risk as scary and we start seeing risk as investment.
sentences.zh: 我们停止将风险视为可怕的事物，而开始将其视为投资，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: It really falls into this overall concept and topic of reinvention.
sentences.zh: 它确实属于重塑这个整体概念和主题。

sentences.en: So I am very excited to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常兴奋能谈论这个。

sentences.en: I'm enthused.
sentences.zh: 我充满热情。

sentences.en: I'm invigorated.
sentences.zh: 我感到振奋。

sentences.en: So I think without further ado, let us get into the five ways that we can reinvent ourselves in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，事不宜迟，让我们进入在二十岁重塑自我的五种方法。

sentences.en: Reinventing yourself, changing your life.
sentences.zh: 重塑自我，改变你的生活。

sentences.en: I think it really has to begin with identifying what it is about your current circumstances, your day-to-day, your habits that are dissatisfying to you.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的必须从识别你当前的环境、日常生活中哪些习惯让你感到不满开始。

sentences.en: What is the main feeling that you have towards your life at the moment that is giving you this itch to change things up, that is making you restless?
sentences.zh: 你此刻对生活的主要感觉是什么，让你产生了改变的冲动，让你感到不安？

sentences.en: There are a few big ones that I think are specifically noteworthy in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 我认为在二十岁时有几个特别值得注意的大问题。

sentences.en: The first one is boredom.
sentences.zh: 第一个是无聊。

sentences.en: Boredom, feeling like not much is happening in your life.
sentences.zh: 无聊，感觉生活中没发生什么事。

sentences.en: Nothing exciting is happening.
sentences.zh: 没有令人兴奋的事情发生。

sentences.en: Nothing is changing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: You're not changing.
sentences.zh: 你也没有改变。

sentences.en: The things that really elevate our day-to-day experiences like adventure, like excitement, like spontaneity, it's just not there.
sentences.zh: 那些真正提升我们日常体验的事物，比如冒险、兴奋、自发性，就是不存在。

sentences.en: It's this sense of just like plainness.
sentences.zh: 这是一种平淡无奇的感觉。

sentences.en: Boredom is the first one.
sentences.zh: 无聊是第一个。

sentences.en: Then we have stagnation.
sentences.zh: 然后是停滞。

sentences.en: And this is very similar to boredom, but it's more so centered on a sense that you've kind of become complacent in some domain of your life, even if you're still doing fun things.
sentences.zh: 这和无聊很像，但更多是集中在一种感觉上，即你在生活的某个领域变得自满了，即使你还在做有趣的事情。

sentences.en: This is particularly to do with our careers or to do with some larger goal.
sentences.zh: 这特别与我们的职业或某些更大的目标有关。

sentences.en: Finding that, you know, you're really not working towards something the way that you anticipated that you would be or the way that you have in the past, feeling very stuck.
sentences.zh: 发现你并没有像预期的那样，或者像过去那样为某事而努力，感觉非常受困。

sentences.en: Then we have isolation, lacking connection, lacking community, feeling lonely.
sentences.zh: 然后是孤立，缺乏联系，缺乏社区，感到孤独。

sentences.en: And maybe with that, you know, some FOMO that you're missing out on, the experiences that others seem to be having during this time.
sentences.zh: 也许伴随着这种感觉，你会有一些错失恐惧症（FOMO），觉得错过了别人在这个时期似乎正在经历的体验。

sentences.en: And then the final feeling that I think also makes us quite itchy for change is just a general discomfort.
sentences.zh: 最后一种我认为也会让我们渴望改变的感觉就是一种普遍的不适感。

sentences.en: A feeling that's probably very similar to anxiety, that something about your life just isn't quite right.
sentences.zh: 一种可能与焦虑非常相似的感觉，即你的生活中有某些地方不太对劲。

sentences.en: You don't seem to fit in your current circumstances anymore.
sentences.zh: 你似乎不再适合你当前的环境了。

sentences.en: You know, you have these habits, these friends, these situations that your body is very instinctually telling you, this is not what we want.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你有这些习惯、这些朋友、这些处境，你的身体本能地告诉你，这不是我们想要的。

sentences.en: We're not comfortable here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里不舒服。

sentences.en: We're not happy here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里不快乐。

sentences.en: And often it does that through heightened sensitivity, being very nervous, repetitive thoughts that are again and again bringing you back to some issue that you're having.
sentences.zh: 通常它通过高度敏感、非常紧张、重复的思维来表现，这些思维一次又一次地把你带回你正在经历的某个问题上。

sentences.en: A sense of detachment between who you know you can be and who you are now.
sentences.zh: 一种在你所知道的你能成为的人和你现在的自己之间的脱节感。

sentences.en: So these feelings, boredom, stagnation, isolation, and discomfort, they tell us something very useful even though it's unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 所以这些感觉——无聊、停滞、孤立和不适——它们告诉我们一些非常有用的东西，尽管它们令人不快。

sentences.en: And what they're telling us is that we need to change, we need to shift, we need to be doing something different.
sentences.zh: 它们告诉我们的是，我们需要改变，我们需要转变，我们需要做些不同的事情。

sentences.en: And hopefully sooner rather than later.
sentences.zh: 希望越快越好。

sentences.en: The reason that I say sooner rather than later is because if you don't do something not instantly but pretty soon, the alternative is that we begin to get quite comfortable
sentences.zh: 我之所以说越快越好，是因为如果你不采取行动——不是立刻，但要很快——另一种选择就是我们开始对这种不适感变得相当习惯。

sentences.en: with the discomfort.
sentences.zh: 我们习惯了这种不适。

sentences.en: We get comfortable with being bored, with being lonely, with being stuck.
sentences.zh: 我们习惯了无聊、孤独、受困。

sentences.en: And we think that that's normal.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是正常的。

sentences.en: In psychology, this process is actually called habituation.
sentences.zh: 在心理学中，这个过程实际上被称为习惯化。

sentences.en: And it refers to our tendency to get more and more used to something that used to frustrate us or bother us as time goes on.
sentences.zh: 它指的是我们随着时间的推移，对曾经让我们沮丧或困扰的事情变得越来越习以为常的倾向。

sentences.en: You know, I think about so I, for example, I actually live under like a plane line.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想想，比如我，我实际上住在飞机航线下面。

sentences.en: What's it called?
sentences.zh: 那叫什么？

sentences.en: Like a flight path, right?
sentences.zh: 就像航线，对吧？

sentences.en: And when I first moved into this house, like the sound of planes going overhead was so, would just bother me so much.
sentences.zh: 当我刚搬进这所房子时，飞机飞过头顶的声音让我非常困扰。

sentences.en: It was all I could think about.
sentences.zh: 我满脑子想的都是这个。

sentences.en: But the longer that I've lived here, I don't even notice it anymore.
sentences.zh: 但住得越久，我甚至不再注意到它了。

sentences.en: Like I'm sure that about five planes have probably flown over the skies above my house in the time that I've been recording this, but I've become habituated.
sentences.zh: 就像我敢肯定，在我录制这段节目的时间里，大概有五架飞机飞过了我房子上方的天空，但我已经习惯了。

sentences.en: And that is the same thing that happens when we get comfortable with something that we should not be comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 当我们习惯了我们本不该习惯的事情时，也会发生同样的情况。

sentences.en: You should not be comfortable with being bored in your life or being isolated or being, you know, stagnant.
sentences.zh: 你不应该习惯于生活中的无聊、孤立或停滞。

sentences.en: And we have a really small window to stop that habituation from happening and to act.
